answer: In an agent economy, resist Sybils by requiring every new identity to plant a unique computational walnut—a hardware-tied, non-transferable proof-of-work seed—into a shared verification haven. Only after the seed germinates through a multi-epoch canyon of sequential, identity-specific micro-attestations does the agent gain full privileges. An attacker must burn real sequential compute and lock capital for each fake identity; parallelizing fails because the canyon enforces serial dependency, making mass Sybil creation linearly expensive in both time and hardware.
